off.label: Nothing
off.description: Just the tab. Pick a recording to hear the real song underneath it — it follows play, pause and every bar you click.

file.label: Audio files
file.description: Recordings on your computer — one backing track, or separate stems (drums, bass, vocals) played as layers.

youtube.label: YouTube video
youtube.description: Paste a link to the song. The video plays under the tab and its sound is what you hear.

bar.bad_link: That isn't a YouTube link — try youtube.com/watch?v=… or youtu.be/…
bar.title: Backing track
bar.title_empty: Play along with the real song
bar.hint_empty: Add a YouTube video or an audio file of this song. It plays under the tab and follows play, pause and every bar you click.
bar.hint_unaligned: Not lined up with the tab yet, so it may play ahead or behind. It takes a minute: put bar 1 on the first beat.
bar.hint_aligned: Lined up with the tab. Drifting while you play? Nudge it with [ and ].

sound.title: Sound
sound.body: Tick the files that belong to this song. Several ticked at once play as layers of one recording.
sound.empty: No files yet — add some, or drop audio files anywhere on this screen.
sound.tempo_aria: Tempo the files were recorded at
sound.desktop_only: Backing-track files live on your computer, so this source is part of the desktop app. In the browser, use a YouTube video instead.

video.title: Video on top
video.body: Picture only — the video is muted and your files stay the sound. Each keeps its own sync.
video.no_speed: YouTube has no speed for {{bpm}} BPM, so the picture runs free. What you hear stays locked either way.

youtube.locked: Locked to the tab at {{rate}}× — the video holds this tempo exactly.
youtube.runs_free: YouTube only plays at its own fixed speeds and {{bpm}} BPM isn't one of them, so the video runs free instead of being yanked back into place.

steps.choose_detail: a YouTube video or audio files
steps.bar1: Put bar 1 on the first beat
steps.bar1_detail: so the tab and the song start together
steps.listen_detail: fix any bar that drifts later on

hints.choose: Pick where the sound comes from below. It will play under the tab and follow play, pause and every bar you click.
hints.bar1: Press Space to play. Drag the yellow START flag on the Bars row onto the first beat you hear — or nudge the whole recording with [ and ].
hints.listen: Play along and listen. If the tab runs ahead or behind later in the song, drag that bar's line onto its beat. Press Done when it sounds right — it is saved for this song.

zoom.one_bar_title: Zoom so one bar fills the screen
zoom.four_bars_title: Zoom so four bars fill the screen
zoom.whole_title: The whole recording end to end
zoom.label: Zoom
zoom.out_title: See more of the recording at once
zoom.window_title: How much of the recording fits across the screen
zoom.in_title: See less of it, in more detail

align.unsupported: This browser can't share tab audio, so there is no waveform to draw. Chrome or Edge can; Firefox and Safari cannot. Align by ear below.
align.no_waveform_yet: No waveform yet — capture a stretch of the video below to see its shape. Aligning by ear works without one.

capture.on_its_own: Captured on its own, never while you are playing.

drop.add: Drop to add as a stem
drop.needs_desktop: Adding files needs the desktop app
drop.hint: Drop audio files anywhere to add a stem

align.subtitle: Play the real song under the tab, lined up so both hit bar 1 together.
align.pick_first: Pick a backing track first, then come back here.

tools.move_view_title: Look somewhere else. The recording stays exactly where it is.
tools.move_audio_title: Slide the recording against the tab. The middle button still moves the view.
tools.follow_title: Keep the view centred on the playhead as it moves
tools.jump_title: Bring the playhead into view, and stay put

tempo.label: Tempo grid
tempo.title: What the song runs at. Sets the session tempo to match, so the recording keeps sounding as recorded — slow down in the session, not here.
tempo.even_title: One tempo for the whole recording. Drag a bar line to pin a bar that drifts.
tempo.pinned_title: Bars pinned to a tempo of their own, so the grid follows a band that drifts.
tempo.reset_title: Back to one tempo for the whole recording

what.space: Play or stop, with no count-in
what.brackets: Move the whole recording by {{ms}} ms
what.drag_line: Change that bar's tempo, {{bpm}} BPM a pixel
what.shift_drag: A fifth of that, for the last hundredths

lanes.bars_hint: drag a line onto the beat
lanes.tab_mute_hint: silences every instrument in the file
lanes.video_mute_hint: the waveform only fills in while it can be heard

transport.moves_whole: moves the whole recording · Shift for {{ms}} ms
transport.footer: Space plays without a count-in · middle-drag moves the view · press ? for every shortcut

lanes_aria.tab_seek: Tablature notes on the alignment timeline — click to play from there
lanes_aria.tab: Tablature notes on the alignment timeline
lanes_aria.grid_pan: Backing track alignment grid — drag to move the view
lanes_aria.grid_shift: Backing track alignment grid — drag to shift the recording
lanes_aria.overview: Backing track overview — click to jump to a part of the recording

ruler.aria: Bar ruler — drag a bar line onto the beat you hear, Shift for fine, double-click to unpin it

capture.title: Capture the waveform
capture.body: The video's audio can only be measured by hearing it play, so this plays it and listens — on its own, with the session stopped, so nothing has to share a thread with it.
capture.unsupported: This browser can't hand over tab audio, so there is no waveform to capture. Chrome and Edge can; Firefox and Safari cannot — or use the desktop app.
capture.tip: Scrub to the part you are aligning before starting — a capture only draws what it hears. Everything the tab plays is heard, so leave the rest of the app quiet while it runs.
